circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has been the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. As the second Middle Eastern circuit to host Formula One races following Bahrain, it preceded the later additions of tracks in Qatar and Saudi Arabia to the championship calendar.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix along with various support series including the Supercars Championship. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification, meeting the highest international safety and facility standards required for premier motorsport events.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the 4. 326 km circuit has a storied history hosting the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct eras. Originally established as the Österreichring, it held the race annually for 18 years until 1987, then returned to the calendar following a reconstruction and renaming as the A1-Ring, serving as the grand prix venue from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, positioned along Baku Boulevard, with a 6. 003 km lap length that ranks as the fourth-longest Formula One venue. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before being rebranded as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onward under the management of the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. The FIA Grade 1-licensed venue accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 Series, endurance racing, and drag racing, with multiple track configurations available for different events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in Catalonia, is a 4. 657 km track featuring a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit positioned near the town of Spa in the Wallonia region, serving as the traditional home of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950. The venue has maintained an unbroken presence on the F1 calendar from 1985 onwards, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometres and serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its role in top-tier single-seater racing, the track has also accommodated various other international motorsport series including sportscars and open-wheel competitions throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix intermittently, with races held from 2004 to 2019 and resuming from 2024. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include additional motorsport events in recent years.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, England, Silverstone Circuit is the traditional home of the British Grand Prix, having inaugurated the event in 1948 and hosting the inaugural World Championship race two years later. After alternating with other British tracks from the mid-1950s through the mid-1980s, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onward, alongside hosting MotoGP racing.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit located near Budapest, Hungary, that hosts the Hungarian Grand Prix. Built in just eight months starting in 1985, it became the venue for Formula One's first Eastern Bloc Grand Prix in 1986, after Bernie Ecclestone's original plans for a Soviet race led to this Hungarian alternative instead.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km track built in 1922 as the world's third purpose-built racing circuit and Europe's oldest on the mainland. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 with only a one-year absence in 1980, the circuit earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" from its characteristic long straights and fast-paced corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track is primarily recognized for hosting Formula One and Super Formula racing championships at the international level.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course navigating through Paradise, Nevada, that incorporates the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its collection of major hotels and casinos. The track features several iconic venues including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as part of its routing through the city streets.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two deceased racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in separate racing accidents in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix intermittently, returning to the calendar in 2015 after a 23-year absence, and now runs under the Mexico City Grand Prix designation since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that hosts the Miami Grand Prix. Spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, the track achieves average qualifying speeds near 139 mph and was specifically designed by Apex Circuit Design for its Formula One debut in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The 3. 337-kilometre street course winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the harbour of the principality. Though officially known as the Circuit de Monaco, it is widely called "Monte Carlo" due to its primary location within that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the Netherlands' grand prix after a decades-long absence, returning to the Formula One calendar in 2021. The partnership between the venue and the sport will conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is positioned near Lusail in northern Qatar, approximately 5. 4 kilometers in length with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aircraft accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track features modern facilities including a karting venue dedicated to fellow Brazilian motorsport legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its 2021 debut, recently welcoming Formula E racing as well.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through downtown Singapore around Marina Bay, incorporating portions of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km track renowned for its balanced design combining extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing various racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and features spectator facilities accommodating approximately 140,700 attendees.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the venue for the United States Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts various international motorsport events including MotoGP's Americas round, NASCAR competitions, and endurance racing championships, establishing itself as a premier destination for multiple racing series in North America.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and multiple prestigious sports car events including Le Mans and Daytona, making him the sole driver to claim titles in both F1 and world sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes on the Formula One grid, having secured six race victories since joining the series in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently drives for the Haas team in Formula One's top-tier championship series.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver competes for Cadillac in Formula One and brings a decade-plus of racing experience along with ten Grand Prix victories. Bottas achieved back-to-back runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship during 2019 and 2020 while driving for Mercedes.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines his role as a reserve for Haas in Formula One with competing in European Le Mans Series prototypes for Nielsen Racing. During 2024 and 2025, he made seven Grand Prix appearances in the top category.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a Grand Prix victory at Monza in 2020 while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: A French-Algerian driver representing France in Formula One, Isack Alexandre Hadjar currently races for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton competes for Ferrari in Formula One, holding an unprecedented seven world championship titles that he shares with Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport's all-time records across multiple categories, including 106 race victories, 104 pole positions, and 207 podium finishes.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One and has an impressive endurance racing pedigree, having claimed victory in the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has secured nine race victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, recently concluded his second stint in Formula One, which spanned from 2022 to 2024. He has since shifted focus to competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship for WRT as a BMW factory driver, while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship title with the team. The accomplished competitor has secured 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix victory with Alpine remains a highlight of his career in the sport.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez, a Mexican driver, currently competes in Formula One for Cadillac. The veteran racer finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while driving for Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having accumulated nine Grand Prix victories since joining the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery for Era Motorsport in the IMSA championship.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One, where he has been competing since 2021 through 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen represents the Netherlands in Formula One while racing for Red Bull Racing, where he has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across 12 seasons, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a racing driver currently functioning as a reserve competitor for Cadillac in Formula One. Between 2022 and 2024, he competed actively in the series, establishing himself as the sole Chinese driver to have participated in the sport's highest level.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing competes as the Enstone-based works team for Renault, rebranded from the Renault F1 Team in 2021 to showcase the Alpine sports car division. The squad secured its only Alpine-era victory through Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix before Renault's factory exit concluded following the 2025 season. Currently powered by Mercedes engines, the team operates under a French licence with Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto as drivers.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-tenured and most accomplished outfit, participating continuously in the World Championship from its inception in 1950. Recognized by their iconic horse emblem, the team remains the most storied competitor in the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the squad commenced racing in 2016 and has competed in Formula One for nearly a decade. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal position, succeeding the founding principal who had overseen operations since the team's establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss motorsport constructor established in 1970, Sauber initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery in 1993. The independent team competed in the championship for over three decades, achieving significant success in endurance racing including a Le Mans victory, before being acquired by Audi in 2024 and subsequently ceasing operations as one of the sport's longest-serving marques.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Bahraini ownership. The team competes in the sport's premier championship and maintains its operations from the McLaren Technology Centre facility.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier. The modern Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley and holding a German racing licence, became a three-way partnership in 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The marque's racing identity is synonymous with the "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024 as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as a sister squad within the Red Bull Formula One structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor established in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the squad functions as Red Bull's sister team within the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England and operating under an Austrian licence, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 under the stewardship of Christian Horner, who led the team until 2025. As one of two racing divisions operated by Red Bull GmbH, the team continues its Formula One campaign following Horner's departure and Laurent Mekies' assumption of the leadership role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head in 1977, stands as a British Formula One constructor and team competing from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters. Emerging from the remnants of Williams's previous failed F1 venture, the operation has since established itself as a significant presence in the sport.
